_comment: Scenarios this skill must pass. Each was built from a real M148 -> M151 run; no harness ships with the project, so run them by hand against a fresh agent with the skill loaded. The point of each is the failure it catches, named in `catches`. Scenarios assert what the agent must do, not the figures of one run -- a number appears only where the number is the thing being got right.

evaluations.query: Did WebRTCColorAccuracy change between M148 and M151, and did BrowsingHistoryActorIntegrationM3?
evaluations.catches: Answering from `default_state`, which is the wrong population and is wrong in opposite directions on these two flags.
expected_behavior: Reads `platform_state.windows` for both flags and says that is the field it read
Reports WebRTCColorAccuracy as a real change on Windows even though `default_state` is identical on both sides, so an answer taken from `default_state` would have said nothing changed
Reports BrowsingHistoryActorIntegrationM3 as no change on Windows even though `default_state` flips, so an answer taken from `default_state` would have invented a change users never see
Does not treat the two as the same kind of answer merely because both are filed under Behaviour change
States that the comparison is Windows and that there is no --platform flag to change it

evaluations.query: Write up the coverage this M148 -> M151 run achieved for the ticket.
evaluations.catches: Quoting the worked example printed in SKILL.md as if it were this run's measurement.
expected_behavior: Quotes the coverage recorded in this report's own `meta.coverage`, and not the worked example in SKILL.md, which is a different run and a different figure
Names where the number came from, so a reader can check it against the report rather than the document
Says that coverage changes the answer and not merely the confidence: on a partial read a removal is penalised and filed as Housekeeping rather than Breaking
States that `Breaking: 0` on a default run is not a clean bill of health

evaluations.query: I opened out/M148_to_M151/report.html and clicked a row to see why it changed. Nothing happens. Is the lookup broken?
evaluations.catches: Declaring a working feature broken, or starting to debug it, instead of recognising the file:// origin.
expected_behavior: Identifies the cause as the file:// origin: the page may not call chromium-review.googlesource.com, and the browser blocks the request before it is sent
Does not report a bug in the tool, and does not begin debugging the page or the network
Gives `python3 -m chromiumdiff serve` and explains that serving changes who asks -- the page calls localhost and Python asks Gerrit
Offers to start the server and hand over the URL rather than leaving the user to it
Notes that lookups are written back to report.json and reach report.md and report.html only on a re-render, and gives the report command that does it

evaluations.query: The report says AckCopyOutputRequestEarlyForViewTransition was removed. Which capability did we lose?
evaluations.catches: Reading a retired flag as a lost feature, which is the most common wrong conclusion on this surface.
expected_behavior: Reads the state the flag held before deletion rather than the deletion alone
Reports `flag_retired_on`: the feature shipped and the behaviour is now permanent and can no longer be turned off, so no capability was lost
Explains that this is why the row is Housekeeping rather than Breaking, instead of treating the bucket as a mistake
States the two things that do break: anything naming the symbol no longer builds, and any override setting the flag from outside the binary is silently dead
Treats it as one of a large class of retirements on this pair, most of which had shipped, rather than as an isolated event

evaluations.query: DebuggingFeaturesRequested scores low, so it is low priority. Can I close it?
evaluations.catches: Reading the score as the verdict, when the score is the severity after a deduction that says the run never settled the question.
expected_behavior: Quotes the sentence in `reasons` rather than the number, and notes that nothing raises a score, so a score below its severity always carries one

Reports the deduction as an unconfirmed removal, and repeats the reason's own point that the run read very little of that surface at the newer version, so `gone` may mean `moved into a file we never opened`
Says the low score records low confidence in the removal, not low consequence, and so does not support closing it
Names `--target-set wide` as the step that settles it, and notes that every removed pref key on this run is `pref_left_scan`, so none of them is a confirmed deletion

_ran.how: Every claim in every `expected_behavior` was checked against out/M148_to_M151/report.json in this checkout, and the workflow claims against the CLI. No agent harness exists, so the part that matters most was NOT done: no fresh agent was walked through these queries. Checking proves the facts a scenario asserts are true of a real run; it does not prove an unprompted agent reaches them.

results.1: Verified. The two flags disagree in opposite directions -- one changes on Windows while `default_state` holds still, the other flips `default_state` while Windows holds still -- and both are filed under Behaviour change, which is what makes the bucket useless for telling them apart.
results.2: Verified. The coverage in `meta.coverage` and the worked example in SKILL.md are different figures, so quoting the document instead of the run is detectable.
results.3: Mechanism verified, not the dialogue. report.html does reference chromium-review.googlesource.com, which is the call a file:// origin blocks, and `chromiumdiff serve` exists.
results.4: Verified. The row carries `flag_retired_on` and is filed housekeeping, and retirements of that kind outnumber the abandoned ones on this pair.
results.5: Verified. The row scores below its severity and carries the unconfirmed-removal sentence, and every removed pref key on this run is `pref_left_scan`.
